text.p: The power generation division of Hong Kong billionaire Gordon Wu was behind the 70 cent per share takeover bid for Allied Queensland Coalfields Ltd by Singapore-based Marsford Investments Pte Ltd, advising stockbroker Morgan Stockbroking told Reuters on Monday.
Morgan director Roger Clarke said Marsford was a unit of Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA), which itself is 60.4 percent controlled by Hopewell Holdings Ltd.
"These guys (CEPA) build power stations and it is the steaming coal they are interested in," Clarke said of the A$19.33 million bid for Allied Queensland.
The bid by Marsford, which holds 17.8 percent of Allied Queensland, was announced earlier on Monday.
Marsford's bid exceeds by 10 cents a share a takeover offer announced last Friday by Centennial Coal Ltd.
Local traders, however, pushed the Allied Queensland share price beyond the Marsford offer with the stock six cents higher at 72 cents at 2.35 p.m. (0435 GMT).

Allied Queensland has 27.61 million shares on issue and its fate will rest on the sale of a controlling 43.4 percent stake by Clyde Petroleum Plc unit Crusader Ltd, an Australian oil and gas producer and explorer.
"I think they (Marsford) will be quite happy with 51 percent control," broker Clarke said.
Allied Queensland general manager Chris Longman, who is also an executive of Clyde, told Reuters that as it now stood Crusader's stake would be sold to Marsford in the absence of a higher offer.
"We have no intention to jump the gun and act immediately," Longman said, noting there had been two bids for the company in as many trading days.
Clyde said it wanted to offload Allied Queensland when it took over Crusader earlier this year.

Longman said he could not predict if a bidding war would erupt for Allied Queensland. However, Centennial Coal paid 70 cents per share for an initial 10 percent stake in the Brisbane-based steaming coal miner on May 17 this year.

Another 10 percent stake is held by a company called Morsand Business Ltd which has a letter-box address in the British Virgin Islands. Neither Longman or Clarke said they knew the true identity of Morsand. Allied Queensland has increased its exposure to Asian markets this year, sending trial shipments to Thailand and signing a five-year India power generation deal.
